page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by a 2.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7H12 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Running on a KVM hypervisor, this instance features 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The instance has a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPUs.

The CPU cache configuration comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 16 MB L3 cache pool. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA vector extensions. It lacks AVX-512 and matrix multiplication extensions. Dedicated CPU scheduling ensures consistent baseline host allocation without burstable credit caps.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded performance alongside limited multi-core throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and single-threaded gzip compression speed of 23.96 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded workloads yield lower results, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 2939.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 1535.77. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 31.36 GB/sec for reads and 16.16 GB/sec for writes. Database operations show modest throughput, with Redis SET performance reaching 3.57 million operations per second and static web serving achieving 4.07 GB/sec.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c6a.xlarge provides balanced resource density for non-memory-intensive applications. It is suitable for lightweight batch processing, single-threaded execution tasks, basic web serving, and general utility workloads where moderate single-core capacity is sufficient and heavy memory bandwidth or massive parallel execution is not required.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It offers 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. The instance operates on a KVM hypervisor without local SSD storage or attached GPU accelerators. Hardware features include 16 MB L3 cache, hardware AES and SHA instruction sets, and standard AVX support. Benchmark testing indicates moderate single-threaded responsiveness, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1305.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.96 GB/sec, alongside weaker multi-core scaling (stress-ng multi-core score of 1535.77) and uncached memory bandwidth (31.36 GB/sec read). This server configuration is best suited for entry-level compute tasks, single-threaded data processing, lightweight web serving, and basic worker nodes.
